title: 7 & 9 F-CLASS TURBINE 1-2 SPACER WHEEL RIM INSPECTION RECOMMENDATIONS
purpose: Communicate inspection recommendations to help mitigate the risk of possible damage to the gas turbine associated with turbine 1-2 spacer wheel rim cracking and possible rim section liberation.
compliance_category_text: Alert - Failure to comply with the TIL could result in equipment damage or facility damage. Compliance is mandated within a specific operating time.
scope_of_work: Upon removal of the turbine shell casing for the hot gas path or major outage, perform a thorough cleaning of the rim of the 1-2 turbine spacer wheel to remove any oil and/or residual debris from the outer surface.
Perform an ultrasonic inspection of the turbine 1-2 spacer wheel rim region (forward and aft rim arms).
service_recommendation_line_items: For select frame 7 and 9 F-class gas turbine rotor 1-2 spacer wheels, perform an ultrasonic inspection of the rim region at the first outage (either hot gas path or major inspection) once the turbine 1-2 spacer wheel has accumulated 80,000 factored fired hours of operation (approximate range for inspection is 80,000 to 96,000 factored fired hours).
Strongly recommended: engage GE's Inspection & Life Extension Services (IL&LES) group to perform the ultrasonic inspection using developed techniques to fully inspect all necessary rim arm regions.
If indications are observed during inspection, contact your GE service representative for assistance with disposition of the findings.
Record TIL disposition in local records and in GE Power ServiceNow (TIL Disposition).
completion_criteria_text: This TIL is considered complete once the inspection mentioned in this recommendations section is completed and dispositioned.
maintenance_trigger_text: Once the turbine 1-2 spacer wheel has accumulated 80,000 factored fired hours of operation (approximate range for inspection is 80,000 to 96,000 factored fired hours).
recommended_interval_or_trigger: Perform inspection at the first outage (either hot gas path or major inspection) once the turbine 1-2 spacer wheel has accumulated 80,000 factored fired hours of operation.
GE recommends performing an inspection of the forward and aft rim arms of any turbine 1-2 spacer wheels having accumulated greater than 80,000 factored fired hours of operation.
usage_counter_requirements_text: Inspection recommended once the turbine 1-2 spacer wheel has accumulated 80,000 factored fired hours of operation (approximate range for inspection is 80,000 to 96,000 factored fired hours).
frame_or_model_applicability_text: Select frame 7 and 9 F-class gas turbine rotor 1-2 spacer wheels with higher operational temperatures and specific environmental conditions. (F-class definition includes specific F, FA, and FB rotors)
hardware_or_part_configuration_text: Turbine 1-2 spacer wheels with higher operational temperatures and specific environmental conditions; rotors operating in higher operational temperatures and humid or corrosive conditions may pose an increased risk of crack initiation and propagation in the rim arms.
prerequisite_outage_or_inspection_contex: At the first outage (either hot gas path or major inspection) after reaching the factored fired hours trigger; scope begins upon removal of the turbine shell casing for the hot gas path or major outage.

parts_referenced.context: turbine 1-2 spacer wheel (rim region; forward and aft rim arms) to be cleaned and ultrasonically inspected
parts_referenced.source_location: RECOMMENDATIONS; SCOPE OF WORK; BACKGROUND DISCUSSION

reference_documents.context: Fleet experience associated with TIL-1937 referenced in background discussion regarding increased risk in higher operational temperatures and humid or corrosive conditions.

configuration_variables: Frame/model: frame 7 and 9 F-class (including specific F, FA, and FB rotors)
Operating environment/conditions: higher operational temperatures; humid or corrosive conditions
Accumulated usage: factored fired hours threshold (>=80,000; inspection range 80,000 to 96,000)
configuration_summary: Applies to select frame 7 and 9 F-class rotor 1-2 spacer wheels, particularly those operating at higher operational temperatures and in humid or corrosive conditions; inspection is triggered by accumulated factored fired hours and performed at the first hot gas path or major inspection outage thereafter.
severity_signals: rim section liberation during full load operation
material ejected into the hot gas path
significant collateral damage to the compressor and turbine sections
failure_consequences: turbine 1-2 spacer wheel rim cracking and possible rim section liberation
significant collateral damage to the compressor and turbine sections of the gas turbine
risk_summary: Cracks can initiate from the internal surface of the turbine 1-2 spacer wheel rim arm and propagate radially and circumferentially outward until the rim can no longer sustain centripetal forces, resulting in rim section liberation and potential significant collateral damage; risk may be increased for rotors operating in higher operational temperatures and humid or corrosive conditions.
missing_information_flags: No specific part numbers, wheel serial ranges, or rotor identification criteria are provided for determining which 'select' frame 7 and 9 F-class units are affected.
No explicit ultrasonic acceptance/rejection criteria or disposition thresholds are provided (only instruction to contact GE if indications are observed).
No explicit follow-on inspection interval after the initial UT is provided (document states further inspections occur as part of rotor life extension processes without specifying timing).

Ultrasonic inspection of the turbine 1-2 spacer wheel rim region can be completed in approximately two shifts (~12-16 hours).
